candidate.answerReason: Subtracting the digit sum from 10a+b gives 9a. Among the nine possible tens digits, only a = 4 produces a result ending in 6. All ten units digits work, agreeing with choice D.

methods.label: Let the units digit cancel
methods.explanation:
Let \(a\) be the tens digit and \(b\) the units digit, so \(1\le a\le9\) and \(0\le b\le9\). The number is \(10a+b\), and subtracting its digit sum gives
\[
(10a+b)-(a+b)=9a.
\]
The units digit \(b\) cancels, so only the tens digit matters. As \(a\) runs from \(1\) through \(9\), the possible results are
\[
9,18,27,36,45,54,63,72,81.
\]
Only \(36\) ends in \(6\), so \(9a=36\) and \(a=4\). Every units digit from \(0\) through \(9\) is then allowed. Thus exactly the numbers \(40,41,\ldots,49\) work, giving \(\boxed{10}\) numbers, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses decimal place value, simple cancellation, and a complete check of nine small multiples.
